articles.title: It’s September. Time to put your knees away | Zoe Williams
articles.summary: From May to August, social media is awash with photos of brown knees. But summer’s almost over and they’re all starting to blur together. It’s the start of September, so time to bid adieu to the classic holiday selfie: two brown knees.
body: Everyone’s knees look the same, which is weird given the sheer variety of body shapes, and everyone’s background is mainly the same: a body of water, conceivably a mountain. There might be a cocktail to the side, but there will never be anything interesting, such as a dog, because that would dispel the serenity. It would be good if the knees were just a frame, and between them some distant, barely legible scene were playing out, such as a sword fight or a harras of many-coloured horses, but that would run counter to the vibe: “I am completely at peace and definitely not seeking out horses and lying near them for clicks.”
points: From May to August, social media is awash with photos of brown knees.
But summer’s almost over and they’re all starting to blur together.

articles.title: Sarah Pound’s creamy, comforting store-bought roast chicken recipes
articles.summary: Using a bachelor’s handbag as a shortcut, the cookbook author shares a cheesy chicken and leek potato bake, a chicken and bacon pie and a rich baked pasta. A store-bought roast chicken is one of my favourite shortcuts, because it’s ready to be shredded and made into something new.
body: Comforting and creamy, this simple and delicious traybake comes with a warning: be very careful not to eat the whole damn thing in one sitting.

Bring a large saucepan of salted water to the boil. Add the potatoes and cook for 10–12 minutes, until just tender when pierced with a knife. Drain and allow to cool slightly. Once cool enough to handle, slice into thin rounds and set aside.

Meanwhile, make the creamy chicken filling. Heat the olive oil and butter in a large frying pan over medium heat. Add the leek and cook, stirring occasionally, for four to five minutes, until softened. Add the garlic and cook for a further minute, until fragrant. Stir in the flour and cook for a minute, then pour in the chicken stock and cook, stirring, for two or three minutes. Slowly whisk in the milk and cream until smooth. Simmer for three or four minutes, until thickened. Add the chicken and cheeses and stir until the cheeses have melted and the sauce is creamy. Season well with salt and pepper.
Preheat the oven to 200C fan. Grease a 25cm × 20cm baking dish.
points: Using a bachelor’s handbag as a shortcut, the cookbook author shares a cheesy chicken and leek potato bake, a chicken and bacon pie and a rich baked pasta.
A store-bought roast chicken is one of my favourite shortcuts, because it’s ready to be shredded and made into something new.

articles.title: A walking tour of Andalucía’s historic white villages: ‘Nightingales serenade us as we wind along lush river valleys’
articles.summary: The famous pueblos blancos in southern Spain’s Sierra de Grazalema natural park teem with wildlife amid a limestone wonderland of peaks. ‘The wind is in from Africa / Last night I couldn’t sleep.” Joni Mitchell has ear-wormed her way into my head as my wife and I step out from Zahara de la Sierra…
body: Either way, Africa feels present as we tramp through the countryside of Andalucía, if only in the wildlife. The painted lady butterflies drifting over the flower-spangled verges, the turtle doves purring from the olive groves and the booted eagle drifting overhead: all are summer visitors recently blown in from the great continent to our south.

It’s day two of our White Villages of the Ronda Mountains walking tour, a self-guided seven-day route from On Foot Holidays that explores this alluring corner of southern Spain. We arrived yesterday by bus from Málaga, winding up through the mountains until the whitewashed dwellings of Zahara appeared like teeth in the hillside ahead. This was the first of the week’s four pueblos blancos, all tucked picturesquely into the natural park’s rugged 51,695 hectares (127,740 acres) of limestone peaks and serpentine river valleys.

I’ve walked with On Foot before, so the routine is familiar: water bottles and packed lunches stashed in daypacks, laminated map around neck on lanyard and route app open on phone (belt-and-braces navigation). Best of all, our luggage is already wending its way by taxi to the next destination.

articles.title: How We Pulled It Off: A Monastery Wedding With Drag Queens in Sintra, Portugal
articles.summary: Two grooms explain how they found a fado performer, flamenco dancers, and drag queens for their 100-guest celebration in the magical Portuguese town.
body: As a couple, Taylor Rains and Carter Joyce have a shared sense of romance, particularly as it relates to travel. “Exploring the world has just helped to deepen our relationship,” says Carter. Since meeting online in 2016, they’ve spent their holiday seasons in Belgium hopping around Christmas markets. It was during their 2022 trip that they became engaged. “We got our mulled wine and got on the Ferris wheel in the main market in Brussels, and Carter proposed,” says Taylor. “It took two full rotations of the Ferris wheel for me to pick my jaw up off the ground.”
Carter Joyce (left) and Taylor Rains met online in 2016, became engaged on a trip to Belgium in 2022, and knew their wedding had to incorporate their love of travel.

It makes sense, then, that they’d want to have their wedding in a storied venue or a gorgeous destination—or both. Their early research found the Charleston -based duo looking into opulent venues, such as the Biltmore Estate in North Carolina, chateaux in France, and villas in Italy. They realized that plotting a destination wedding would allow them to curate a gorgeous experience for their loved ones.

articles.title: All the Best Looks From the 2026 Venice Film Festival
articles.summary: As the 2026 Venice Film Festival kicks off this week, all eyes will be on the red carpet—with the likes of George and Amal Clooney, Claire Foy, and Robert Pattinson arriving in the Italian city. See all the best fashion from Venice Film Festival so far.
body: Red carpet lovers, it’s your lucky day: The 2026 Venice Film Festival has officially arrived.

The film roster for this year’s festival has plenty of buzzy projects to take in: Among them is Martin McDonagh’s Oscar-tipped black comedy Wild Horse Nine; Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime; a Robert Pattinson-led portrait of To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen; and Bunker, Florian Zeller’s marital drama starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

Better year, however, is what all of these A-listers will be wearing on the step and repeat for the splashy premieres. This is, after all, the festival that last year offered the first glimpses of new-era Chanel, Dior, Versace and Bottega Veneta before their respective runway debuts, and which has given us Lady Gaga’s feathered Valentino couture gown in 2018 and Zendaya’s wet-look Balmain dress in 2021, among other standout moments.

articles.title: A Witchy Guide on What to Do for Salem’s 400th Anniversary
articles.summary: Vogue’s go-to astrologer speaks to a handful of modern witches living in and around Salem to get their tips on how to experience the city’s spiritual side.
body: In 2026, the city of Salem is celebrating its 400th anniversary—but as the season of the witch approaches this fall, tourism is already ramping up. It’s little surprise: Despite Salem’s scandalous history of witch hunts and trials that loom over its origin story, today, it’s a vibrant city where everyone is accepted and embraced, including modern witches and spiritual healers.

As an astrologer with deep connections in the modern witchcraft community, it’s one of my favorite places in America—and if you’re going to visit Salem to celebrate the city, there are many stores and historical landmarks I’d recommend you check out. Find them all below—plus several other favorites that witchy residents of Salem recommended to me.

The owner of Ascend Get Lifted, Carmelo Aresco, is a lightworker whose shop has everything your magical heart might crave—from potent crystals (I own an onyx apple among other precious findings I’ve bought there) to home goods. Ascend also offers tea leaf and tarot readings, healing sessions, and aura photos—all by excellent practitioners, and right in the middle of bustling Essex Street.

articles.title: Meet Alex Eala, the Tennis Player Creating a Sensation With Every Match
articles.summary: The 21-year-old Filipina, ranked 18th in the world, has energized an entire country.
body: Eala—who plays her first match at the 2026 US Open tonight at Armstrong Stadium, the venue’s marquee court—has embraced this wave of growing fanfare ever since her breakthrough at the 2022 US Open, where she won the girls’ singles title to become her nation’s first Grand Slam champion. In the year and a half since her breakout semifinal run at last year’s Miami Open—where she stunned three Grand Slam champions along the way—Eala’s unprecedented success has not only crowned a new sporting icon for the Philippines; it’s sparked a nationwide embrace of tennis.

“At first, it took me quite aback because I couldn’t understand how [Filipinos] could feel so deeply or so passionately towards the work that I do,” Eala admits over coffee after a late-night win in Toronto. “It was hard for me to wrap my head around the fact that I was famous.” Over time, though, she has come to realize and accept that she now occupies the same position for her young fans as Eala’s own childhood idols, Maria Sharapova and Li Na, did for her.
